cells.tense: The clearing is here now, and the growing in it is being tended by you.
cells.ask: Point one clear hour this week at something still growing, give it that and no more, and let the rest of the day take care of itself. Hold it where the next step comes easy.
cells.core:
Something got cleared out, and you didn't rush in to put it back. That's the part worth noticing. What's starting to grow now is getting your attention without your grip — you water it and step back, and it keeps going without you standing over it.

That's the whole trick of it, and you already have it. Care that doesn't drain you is care you can actually keep, so the space you're holding stays open instead of tightening. Nothing has to be locked down for the thing to survive. What you're holding is allowed to hold itself up for an hour while you do something else. That isn't neglect. It's how you keep this.
cells.sheetLine: You're watering what's growing and not standing over it.
cells.place: in the sudden clearing where what could not hold has gone

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead, you can already see a version of this that hasn't happened yet, and you are holding on to it so it comes true.
cells.ask: Pick the one growing thing you're watching hardest and hand it to someone else for the day, without checking on it. Take the day back for yourself.
cells.core:
You can see how this should go, and you're working hard to make it. Before anyone's asked, you've already leaned in — checking, correcting, holding it together so it doesn't fall. You'd call it care, and part of it is. But the grip has grown past the thing it's holding.

The clearing already happened here, and you're still bracing for the next one. What you're doing right now isn't growing anything. It's standing guard. The return isn't to stop caring — it's to keep the next move to what's actually in front of you, and let the step after it stay unfinished until you get there. Watch how much easier today is to carry that way.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding on too hard for anything to grow straight.

cells.tense: The door you're standing at has been behind you for a while now, and nothing in front has moved.
cells.ask: Water one growing thing for ten minutes today, on your own, and stop when the timer goes off. Then say out loud what you noticed, even if the answer is nothing.
cells.core:
You're holding a cleared-out space like it's a room you're not allowed to use yet. Nothing gets planted, nothing gets tended, and it all reads as fine from the outside — you look steady, capable, like someone who doesn't need anything growing. Underneath, there's nothing you're feeding.

What makes that bearable is usually distance. If you don't need anyone, nothing can be taken. But a line of growth you actually want is still there, no matter how long it's been quiet. Anything small you'd like to still be true in a year counts. Give it the ten minutes and stop there, whatever happens in them. Something gets picked up the hour you stop watching for it, not before.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing's growing and you've arranged it that way.

cells.tense: They already call you the one who keeps everyone steady, and you didn't sign up for the job.
cells.ask: List the three things you regularly hold up for other people. Cross off one you didn't agree to, and tell that person you're off it, this week, in one plain sentence.
cells.core:
People bring you their problems and you take them. You're the one in the room who absorbs what's coming so nobody else has to — and you feel it as wearing down, a load you didn't pick. What they see and what you're carrying don't match.

The clearing already happened around you; what's left is a role you're still holding in place. Nobody assigned it. It got handed over because you were there and kept answering. Naming one thing as yours is what takes it out of the room's hands — say it was a choice and you can choose again. Then stop doing that one. Staying steady stays with you, and you get to decide who it's for.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one holding it up, and you didn't choose to be.
